question.problem:
Use the flux form of Green's theorem to calculate the flux of the vector field

$$
F(x,y)=⟨{e}^{y}-4xy,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡x+2xy⟩
$$

through the boundary of the rectangle $-1\le x\le 1,-1\le y\le 0.$
question.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $F=P\,i+Q\,j,$ and $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first derivatives on an open region containing $D,$ then the flux form of Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∬}_{D}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}A,
$$

which is equivalent to

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14129319/assets/9e0bf7b88eadd199edc1997410b7ddbaa74b204e7d0f8afef7c9b17c28d8f8dc.png)

We have that $P(x,y)={e}^{y}-4xy$ and $Q(x,y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x+2xy.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=-4y,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =2x.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the rectangular region $D$ as follows:

$$
D=\{(x,y):-1\le x\le 1,\,-1\le y\le 0\}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem in flux form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s & ={∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx \\  & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-4y+2x)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{-1}^{1}(2x-4y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}[{x}^{2}-4yx]_{-1}^{1}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}[({1}^{2}-4y(1))-((-1)^{2}-4y(-1))]\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}-8y\,dy \\  & =-4{y}^{2}\,{|}_{-1}^{0} \\  & =0-(-4(-1)^{2}) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
